item.text: {"analysis":"Increasing training negatives from 128 to 512 failed to improve validation: pinned-host macro HR@10 fell from the supplied reference 0.5312 to 0.505, a decrease of 0.0262. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.545, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.580, Electronics 0.395, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.500. Prior category scores were not supplied, so category-specific regressions cannot be established. Macro HR@20 was 0.6375 and NDCG@10 was 0.3254. The trial completed successfully using 508.52 allocated GPU-seconds. The result does not support the hypothesis that stronger negative competition improves this configuration; the cause of degradation is unverified. More negatives change the sampled classification objective, and duplicate negatives remain allowed. Treat 512 negatives as an unsuccessful setting relative to the supplied reference.","code_summary":"One independent ConvRec model is trained per category, with exactly one selected checkpoint loaded per category at inference. Each network uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations 1,2,4,8 repeated twice, two-head causal attention with jointly learned relative-distance bias, layer normalization, and jointly learned item bias. Training uses up to 100 history items, prefix augmentation, and 512 uniform negatives per history, excluding its full training history and sharing negatives across supervised transitions. The 513-class cross-entropy uses recency weights with half-life 10 and per-history normalization. AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, gradient clipping, seed 42, and validation checkpoint selection remain unchanged. Dataset routing and predictor generation preserve the trained architecture; no ensembles or separately fitted scorers are used."}
